messages:

Subject: MAP request: on-prem & private lead times + GPU sizing buffer

Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. ACME would like a short mutual action plan (MAP) we can share with procurement that spells out the evaluation milestones and the close timeline for Dedicated/Private deployments. Two specific asks:

- Can you provide realistic lead times for Private (VPC + cloud-hosted private control plane) vs fully on-prem (hardware order, install, and acceptance)?
- We need a recommended GPU pool sizing starter and explicit guidance on a staging buffer (we want to avoid a late-stage shortage).

Goal: procurement wants target sign-off and PO by the end of June so engineering can schedule hardware and on-prem install windows. Please include acceptance criteria for the on-prem rollout (SLA, security evidence, SOC2 gate) and any evaluation gating (throughput/latency targets) we should include in the MAP.

If you can send a one-pager and a sizing worksheet we can attach to the procurement packet that would be ideal.

Thanks — look forward to the MAP draft.

Alice Jensen

Subject: Re: MAP request: on-prem & private lead times + GPU sizing buffer

Alice —

Appreciate the clear asks. I put together a concise MAP draft and a sizing worksheet (attached) with our recommended staging buffer. High-level summary below; full details in the attached PDF and workbook.

Key lead-time guidance (typical):
- Redwood Hosted / Dedicated (reserved capacity): near-term — reserved pools can be provisioned within 1–2 weeks after contract execution and payment, with optional burst capacity the same day in many regions.
- Redwood Private (VPC-managed control plane): 4–6 weeks after contract + network prep (we'll need a single maintenance window for connectivity & routing).
- On-prem (hardware + on-prem package): 10–14 weeks from PO for hardware (dependent on vendor lead times) + 1–2 weeks for on-site install + 1 week for acceptance QA (so budget ~12–17 weeks total).

GPU pool sizing & staging buffer (recommendations):
- Starter configuration for pilot: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs (sustained inference for low-latency PoC).
- Production initial tranche: 12–16 GPUs (split across 2 availability zones or racks) depending on concurrency targets.
- Staging buffer: add 25% capacity above expected concurrency for the first 90 days to handle peak eval traffic and model tuning.
- Contingency: enable cross-region fallback to Dedicated pool in the first 60 days in case on-prem acceptance lags.

Acceptance gating & eval milestones (proposed MAP items):
1) Week 0–2: Access & onboarding — credentials, network tests, sample inference sanity checks.
2) Week 2–4: Performance eval — end-to-end throughput, 95th pct latency target (e.g., <300ms for 1k-token prompts), cost/per-token profiling.
3) Week 4–6: Security & compliance handoff — SOC2 evidence, KMS integration, audit log check.
4) Week 6–8: Production readiness sign-off (can be earlier for Hosted/Dedicated).

I've attached: Redwood_MAP_v1.pdf (one-pager MAP) and GPU_Sizing_Worksheet.xlsx (worksheet with three sizing scenarios and cost estimates).

Proposed next steps: 30-min alignment call Friday 16 May 10:00 PT to agree on the PO target and acceptance criteria. If that works I'll invite Marissa (onboarding lead) and Ben (solutions) to the call.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP request: on-prem & private lead times + GPU sizing buffer

Hannah / team —

Quick internal alignment memo to add technical acceptance criteria and a sizing option set that ACME can pick from. Sending so we can finalize the MAP before Friday's call.

Acceptance criteria (technical):
- Functional: sample workloads (3 prompts, 5k tokens total) run with no errors and deterministic model versioning across requests.
- Performance: 95th percentile latency < 300ms for the pilot prompt set at target concurrency; throughput target = 200 tokens/sec per GPU as baseline (verify in PoC).
- Reliability: KV cache warm-up < 30s for typical context reuse patterns; continuous batching not to increase 95th pct by >20%.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 docs provided + KMS integration tested; network ACLs validate return paths.

Sizing options (simple):
- Minimal PoC: 4 GPUs (A100 equiv) — dev + small pilot (expected concurrency 20–40 r/s).
- Standard initial: 12 GPUs — supports 150–250 concurrency depending on model/seq length.
- Aggressive production: 24 GPUs — target for enterprise peak loads; recommended if ACME wants <100ms target for short prompts.

Staging buffer guidance:
- Recommend +25% for PoC -> Standard transition; +40% if model tuning expected to spike token usage.
- Recommend scheduling hardware delivery windows with vendor flexibility (split the initial order into 70/30 tranches) to reduce lead-time disruption.

Operational notes for MAP:
- Add an explicit fallback clause: If on-prem acceptance extends beyond 8 weeks from planned acceptance, enable Redwood Dedicated routing for 60–90 days at pre-negotiated rates.
- Add measurement checkpoints at Weeks 2, 4, and 6 with short QA signoffs (1–2 reviewers).

I'll sync with Ben for the cost delta table and Karthik on the deployment checklist before Friday.

-Marissa
Senior Onboarding Manager — Redwood Inference
